name: Forward Distribution Hub

placement_rationale.text: Supply/depot nodes sit back from contact for survivability — a hub feeds many units at once, so a single hit here cascades far wider than a single gun's loss, exactly as the asset's own text argues. At 80km the hub sits inside doctrine.md §2's medium/long-range strike layer (10-150+km) but well beyond FPV range and most counter-battery reach, matching the op_deep band's purpose. Confirmed plausible at current depth, no change.

short_role: Forward distribution point that breaks bulk supply down into brigade- and battalion-sized loads for onward movement toward the line.
characteristics: Sits beyond most FPV and short-range counter-battery reach, inside longer-range strike depth
Feeds forward via a rotating pool of soft-skin and armored logistics vehicles
A single hit here cascades into shortages across every unit it feeds — a higher-value target than any one gun
employment_notes: Dispersed and camouflaged rather than concentrated in one visible depot — the doctrine that punished massed Cold War-era supply dumps applies even more sharply now that reconnaissance drones and deep-strike systems can reach this depth. Convoys forward from here run on staggered schedules for the same reason artillery displaces after firing.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional logistics doctrine could afford larger, more centralized rear depots because the depth at which they sat was genuinely safe from routine engagement. Persistent overhead ISR and medium/long-range strike systems have pushed that safety margin outward and made dispersion — smaller, more numerous, more mobile distribution points — the norm even at operational depth, not just at the front.
